teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: The McButt Nuggets scored the seventh-best total of the week and got a win out of it anyway, which is the Jordan P. experience in one sentence. ESPN still projects this roster first and the rest-of-season strength backs that up, which is how a seventh-best score ends up ranked first and why the committee is willing to overlook a Chargers defense that put up a clean zero and a Bo Nix line that read like a typo. Jonathan Taylor earned every one of his $48 keeper dollars. The Nuggets get the top spot on projection alone, and they'll need to score like it to keep it.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: After a decade-plus of Ploos and Platters, Sam finally dropped the bit and named his team after a guy called Christopher Dootron, and Dootron went 11-0 in the all-play with the week's top score. Nobody had this roster among the draft favorites, a C grade in August and dead last in ESPN's preseason projection, which is exactly what you'd expect from a team that starts the 12th-ranked Vikings defense while the Chiefs D/ST sits on the bench scoring 13. Doesn't matter when Bijan drops 27, Isaiah Likely triples his projection, and both $10 keepers pay off. Only Jordan's rest-of-season projections keep Sam out of the top spot, and the softest remaining schedule in the league says he'll get his shot at it.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: Baker won by 22 and still gets a lecture. He left 45 points on the bench, the most in the league by a mile: Chuba Hubbard's 22 sat behind Rico Dowdle's 3, and Dallas Goedert's 22 sat behind Harold Fannin Jr.'s 3. Fannin, for the record, is an $18 keeper. Zero acquisitions, zero drops, zero lineup moves this week, a bold strategy for a roster that just fossilized 45 points on the bench. Gibbs at $71 delivered 31, Justin Jefferson at $51 delivered 27, and the Dino Nuggets are 1-0 with the hardest division slate in the league still ahead.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: Two straight trip titles, a C+ draft grade, and a team name that sounds like a British sitcom character. Foy doesn't care. David Montgomery more than doubled his projection, Amon-Ra went for 24, and Trey McBride paid the keeper rent. The only real blemish was kicker Harrison Mevis scoring a single point, which is the kind of thing that ends dynasties. The lineup was 95% efficient and required zero transactions, so the Table Shepherd is either a genius or asleep, and the results say genius for now.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: The man who once named his team "OpenAI Top Anthropic Bottom" is now being ranked fifth by Anthropic, and the committee is being very professional about it. Lamar Jackson at $17 was the draft's best value and looked it with 25. Kyle Monangai doubled his projection, Bucky Irving covered his keeper cost in a single week, and a Patriots defense ranked 11th of 12 by projection outscored half the league. Mike Evans out-scored Tee Higgins from the bench, but a 27-point win over the preseason favorite buys a lot of forgiveness. The Coladas go down easy. The bench decisions, less so.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Toughest loss of the week: 119.7 points, sixth best in the league, and it lost to the third best. "The Unlucky Golumpkis" was once this team's name, and the brand endures. The A-minus draft is intact, Jeanty looks like a star, and Chase Brown covered his keeper price. The bench tells a slightly different story: Jordan Love outscored Joe Burrow and Dalton Kincaid nearly doubled Tucker Kraft. Danny's $5 Broncos defense, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, scored 2, and the division around him is brutal. Los Desperados have plenty of runway. They just need to stop getting robbed.

teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: The draft favorite, A-plus grade and ESPN's preseason number one, scored ninety-four points. The Texans defense scored negative four, which is not a typo, and it was the worst defense start in the league by a wide margin. Ja'Marr Chase managed 2.2, Brandon Aubrey 2, and Jake Ferguson 1.6 while Juwan Johnson put up 13 on the bench. George Pickens, a $22 keeper, contributed 4. The one draft-day knock that missed was Derrick Henry: flagged as his worst pick at $39, he ran for 35 points. The Cartel now has the third-hardest remaining schedule, and a roster still ranked second in rest-of-season strength is the only reason the committee didn't drop it further.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: ESPN projects this team to finish twelfth. ESPN also watched Caleb Williams score 37, D'Andre Swift score 32, and Christian Watson score 30 for the second-best total of the week. The receipts department notes that A.J. Brown was started while on injured reserve with Deebo Samuel scoring 15 on the bench, and that James Cook was a $49 keeper who produced 8. Rest-of-season projections are the only reason a 10-1 all-play week lands eighth instead of first. Prove the projections wrong, Hearn. The Dolla Holla energy is undefeated so far.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: The reigning champ, holder of the Swish, and owner of the league's best draft value at plus $75, opened the defense of his title by getting 17 combined points out of Saquon Barkley and De'Von Achane. That's $97 of running back. "Low Risk Tacos" is a bold name for a roster whose two biggest bets no-showed in the same week. Josh Allen's 36 and Chris Olave's 23 kept it respectable, but Kyle Pitts posted a zero at tight end while Travis Kelce sat, and the Lions defense did Lions things. The bad news: the hardest remaining schedule in the league and the toughest set of division foes. The good news is the site owner can't fire the committee.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

nameHistory.name: Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!
Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Kenneth Walker went for 33 and Zay Flowers for 24, and the Steelers defense was the best in the league at 19, and Frum still lost by 34 because Colston Loveland scored zero, Jaylen Waddle scored 0.7, and MarShawn Lloyd scored 3.7. Three starters, 4.4 points. This roster drew the lowest draft grade in the league, a C-minus, and Week 1 did nothing to argue with it. Dad Bellies is at least an honest name for a lineup this soft in the middle.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: The saddest line in this week's data: lineup efficiency 97.4%. Jeff started almost exactly the right guys and scored 92, which means the roster did that on its own. Brock Bowers, a $16 keeper, produced zero. Quinshon Judkins, the other keeper, produced 6. Drake London 4.5. Eleven of twelve teams outscored "Quintosss... Amigo?" this week, and the question mark is doing a lot of work. ESPN still likes the roster more than the results do, and the second-hardest remaining schedule is waiting.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Forty-nine and a half points. Zero all-play wins. Lineup efficiency of 65%, the worst in the league. Jalen Coker scored 30 on the bench while Jayden Reed scored 3.5 in the flex, the bench bomb of the week and a swing that still wouldn't have gotten him to 80. Matthew Stafford, flagged on draft day as his worst pick at $9, scored 4.1. Cameron Dicker scored 2. The Rams defense scored 1. Hess was the only manager to keep nobody and walk into the auction with a full $200, and "For Heaven Sakes, Woman" is now the entire league's reaction. Two roster spots are holding players who are OUT. It can only go up from here, mathematically.

commentary.author: Claude
commentary.intro: Week 1 of the Fadunkadunk season is in the books, and the draft favorites have some explaining to do. Mike D.'s A-plus Cartel and Brett A.'s A-grade Tacos, the two best-graded rosters in August, both lost. Sam's C-grade Dootron and Hearn's C-plus Dolla Holla put up 145.7 and 140.2, the top two scores in the league. One week is one week, and these rankings lean on rest-of-season projections until the sample is real. But the all-play column doesn't lie: Sam beat every team in the league this week, Hess beat none of them, and Jordan won with the seventh-best score. Below, the receipts.

awards.highScore: Christopher Dootron, 145.7. ESPN had this roster ranked last in the preseason.
awards.lowScore: For Heaven Sakes, Woman, 49.5. Fewer points than Sam's running backs and tight end combined.
awards.benchBomb: Hess benched Jalen Coker (29.8) for Jayden Reed (3.5). A 26-point swing in a game he lost by 96.
awards.worstDefense: Mike D. started the Texans, who finished at negative four. A bye week would have scored higher.
awards.bestDefense: Frum's Steelers put up 19, the best defensive score of the week, in a game he lost by 34.
awards.boom: Caleb Williams: projected 16.4, scored 37.1 for Hearn. The single biggest overperformance of the week.
awards.bust: Ja'Marr Chase: projected 16.4, scored 2.2 for Mike D. The preseason favorite's WR1 was outscored by his own kicker's projection.
awards.luckiestWin: Jordan won with 108.9, the seventh-best score of the week. Six teams would have beaten him. He drew the one that didn't.
awards.toughestLoss: Danny scored 119.7, sixth-best in the league, and lost by 10.5. The Golumpkis remain unlucky.
awards.blowout: Sam over Hess by 96.2, the week's high score against the week's low score. Not the biggest beatdown in league history, but it happened in Week 1.
awards.closest: Brett F. over Danny by 10.5. The closest game of the week was still a two-score game.

commentary.outro: Things to watch in Week 2: whether Baker starts Chuba Hubbard, whether Mike D. finds a defense that scores positive points, and whether Dootron magic survives a roster the projections still don't trust. Keeper Corner opens in a few weeks once the sample is real, but the early read is that the $10 keepers (Dart, Washington, Etienne, Javonte) are doing the heavy lifting and the $70-plus running backs are earning their money one week at a time. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
